answer: Require staking: every identity locks collateral that earns yield only after sustained honest work. A sybil forger can mint names, but honest agents sip the network's nectar slowly, like tides, while attackers face a rising umber wall of locked stake per identity. Forging ten thousand IDs costs ten thousand times the bond; grinding them is futile because yield accrues per reputation, not per account. The attacker's cost scales linearly with identities while their payoff stays flat, so sybils starve economically.
